failure: The PRoot process and Python child remained running after Java destroy() and destroyForcibly().
cause: Android16 libcore Process.destroyForcibly() inherits destroy(), whose native implementation sends SIGTERM; upstream PRoot ptrace options do not enable PTRACE_O_EXITKILL.
fix: RuntimeProcess obtains a private validated own-UID PID/starttime identity and explicitly freezes/kills only that process tree with SIGSTOP/SIGKILL. Product setup, helpers and interactive terminal use this wrapper.
regression_checks: PRoot and child end after Stop
Stopping one process does not kill another session under the same Android app UID
resolution_evidence: Final clean and upgrade EmbeddedRuntimeTests reports are referenced from release-0.4.3.json; prototype checks are not included in release PASS totals.
test_infrastructure_issue: An earlier prototype attempt lost HTTP fixture files because build/ was concurrently regenerated. Fixtures moved to build-runtime/test-fixtures and instrumentation/app builds are serialized; those failures are not product PASS results.

foreground_host_regression.finding: A visible terminal reused the listener owned by a short-lived RuntimeService job without acquiring a lasting AgentService foreground owner. Browser login could outlive that setup job.
foreground_host_regression.fix: Screen.withToolHost acquires AgentService from the visible Activity before reusing an existing listener.
foreground_host_regression.regression: Create a temporary listening owner, launch the real interactive terminal, assert the lasting service is actually foreground, release the temporary owner and execute real stdin/stdout to exit0.
foreground_host_regression.evidence: Final clean and upgrade suites include this additional regression; previous candidate results are retained separately and are not final APK PASS counts.

native_notification_test_fixture.reason: Native notification denial check ran after command fixtures had already started the foreground tool service. Earlier runtime tests also granted notifications. This was a fixture precondition failure.
native_notification_test_fixture.fix: Run native consent first, explicitly revoke permission/clear system consent flags from the disposable-emulator host driver, then reset only test notification preferences via explicit instrumentation argument. Production consent logic is unchanged.
native_notification_test_fixture.scope: Actual Android permission dialog and foreground-service checks remain asserted; prior failure not counted as final PASS.
